_note: Head-to-head pages (/vs/<a>-vs-<b>/). Specs, prices, differences, table and radar come from products.json; only editorial text lives here.

matchups.intro: The two 1 kWh stations most shoppers compare at $499. The Jackery is lighter and has the bigger review history; the EcoFlow has more output, a faster UPS and more solar input.
matchups.choose_a: You'll carry it often (23.8 lb vs 26.7 lb), want a slightly bigger battery (1,070 vs 1,024 Wh) and value Jackery's long track record — 3,600+ ratings.
matchups.choose_b: You want more power (1,800 W vs 1,500 W, 3,600 W surge), a 10 ms UPS instead of 20 ms, 500 W solar instead of 400 W and a fourth AC outlet.
matchups.bottom_line: For home backup, the DELTA 3 Classic. For camping and carrying, the Explorer 1000 v2.
faq: Which charges faster?
Both get close to an hour: the Jackery fills in 1 hour in emergency mode, the EcoFlow reaches 80% in 45 minutes.
Which is better for a CPAP?
Both run a CPAP for two or more nights. The EcoFlow's 10 ms UPS switch is a little faster if the power drops overnight.
Can either be expanded?
No. The Jackery 1000 v2 and the DELTA 3 Classic both have fixed capacity.

matchups.intro: Two of the newest 1 kWh stations, both about $500, both around 25 lb with 10 ms UPS. Anker wins on output and charging speed; BLUETTI on solar input.
matchups.choose_a: You want the most power (2,000 W vs 1,800 W), the fastest wall charge (full in 49 minutes) and a time-of-use mode that saves on electricity.
matchups.choose_b: You'll charge mostly from solar: it accepts 1,000 W vs 600 W, and it's a little smaller at 17 liters with a 30 dB silent mode.
matchups.bottom_line: Grid charging and higher loads: Anker C1000 Gen 2. Solar-first: BLUETTI Elite 100 V2.
faq: Which lasts longer?
Both are rated for 4,000 cycles to 80% capacity and carry 5-year warranties.
Which runs a microwave better?
The Anker, with 2,000 W continuous. Many 1,000 W microwaves draw about 1,500 W, which both can handle.
Which is lighter?
They're nearly identical: 24.9 lb for the Anker and 25 lb for the BLUETTI.

matchups.intro: Two 300 W, 290 Wh LiFePO4 stations. The Jackery is Amazon's best seller and costs $70 less; the Anker adds a UPS, faster charging and powerful USB-C.
matchups.choose_a: You want the proven best seller for less money ($259 vs $330), and 4,000 cycles (to 70%) with a 7.5 lb body.
matchups.choose_b: You charge laptops over USB-C (two 140 W ports), want a 10 ms UPS, a third AC outlet, 80% in 50 minutes and a whisper-quiet 25 dB fan.
matchups.bottom_line: Simple camping power: Jackery 300. Desk UPS and laptops: Anker C300.
faq: Which recharges faster?
The Anker: 80% in 50 minutes vs about four hours for the Jackery from the wall.
Can either run a CPAP?
Both can run a CPAP without heat for about one night; with the heated humidifier on, expect only 2–3 hours.
Which has the better warranty?
Anker lists 5 years; the Jackery listing shows 2 years.

matchups.intro: Two small stations with 600 W output, 10 ms UPS and fast charging, about $300 each. EcoFlow can add batteries; BLUETTI costs less and surges higher.
matchups.choose_a: You may want more capacity later (up to 858 Wh with extra batteries), prefer three AC outlets, a one-hour full charge and Wi-Fi app control.
matchups.choose_b: You want the lower price ($280 vs $299), 1,500 W Power Lifting for resistive loads and 140 W USB-C.
matchups.bottom_line: Buy the RIVER 3 Plus if expansion matters; otherwise the Elite 30 V2 is the better deal.
faq: Which is better as a UPS for a PC?
The RIVER 3 Plus includes a USB cable so your PC or NAS can shut down cleanly on low battery.
Which is lighter?
The EcoFlow: 7.7 lb vs 9.5 lb.
Which takes more solar?
The EcoFlow: 220 W vs 200 W.

matchups.intro: Two compact 2 kWh stations. Anker's S2000 costs $200 less, sips 6 W at idle and has 8 outlets; Jackery's 2000 v2 has more output and surge.
matchups.choose_a: You want the best value ($700 vs $899), long outage runtime thanks to a 6 W idle draw, 8 AC outlets, a 10 ms UPS and a 10,000-cycle battery.
matchups.choose_b: You need to run bigger loads (2,200 W vs 1,500 W, 4,400 W surge) and want a 12 V car port, which the S2000 lacks.
matchups.bottom_line: For most outage backup, the S2000. For higher-draw appliances, the Explorer 2000 v2.
faq: Which runs a fridge longer?
The S2000, thanks to its 6 W idle draw; Anker claims up to 35 hours for a typical fridge.
Which is lighter?
The Anker at 35.7 lb vs 39.5 lb.
Do either take much solar?
No, both top out at 400 W.

matchups.intro: Same 1,024 Wh battery and 1,800 W inverter. The DELTA 3 adds an expansion port, two more AC outlets and alternator charging for $100 more.
matchups.choose_a: You want to expand to 5 kWh later, need six AC outlets and 13 outputs, or plan to charge from a vehicle's alternator.
matchups.choose_b: You want the same core power station for $100 less and don't need expansion.
matchups.bottom_line: Most buyers should get the Classic; pay for the DELTA 3 only if you'll use the expansion port.
faq: Can the DELTA 3 Classic use extra batteries?
No. EcoFlow says it isn't compatible with DELTA 2 or DELTA 3 extra batteries.
Do they charge at the same speed?
Both reach 80% in about 45 minutes from the wall; the DELTA 3 can also combine wall and solar for a full charge in 56 minutes.
Which has the better UPS?
The Classic lists a 10 ms UPS. The DELTA 3's listing doesn't state a switchover time.

matchups.intro: Two 3.6 kWh, 3,600 W home-backup stations. The Jackery is newer, lighter and cheaper; the EcoFlow takes more solar and expands further.
matchups.choose_a: You want the lower price ($1,709 vs $1,899), a lighter unit (77 vs 99 lb), a 30 A RV outlet and a 6,000-cycle battery.
matchups.choose_b: You have a big solar array (1,600 W vs 1,000 W), want to charge from a 240 V outlet or EV station, or plan to scale to 25 kWh.
matchups.bottom_line: For most homes, the HomePower 3600 Plus. For solar-heavy or large expandable systems, the DELTA Pro.
faq: Can either power a house?
With a transfer switch, both can run selected circuits. Pair two units for 7,200 W and 240 V.
What about idle draw?
The Solar Lab measured about 34 W for the Jackery 3600 Plus with the inverter on; switch AC off when it isn't needed.
Do they have wheels?
Yes, both roll on wheels with a pull handle.

matchups.intro: BLUETTI's older and newer 1 kWh stations. The AC180 is $50 cheaper with a bit more capacity; the Elite 100 V2 is 12 lb lighter with double the solar input.
matchups.choose_a: You want the most Wh for the money (1,152 Wh for $449) and Amazon as the seller.
matchups.choose_b: You'll carry it or charge from solar: 25 lb vs 37.4 lb, 1,000 W vs 500 W solar, a 10 ms UPS instead of 20 ms and 3,600 W surge.
matchups.bottom_line: Stationary backup on a budget: AC180. Everything else: Elite 100 V2.
faq: Which charges faster from the wall?
Both reach 80% in about 45 minutes.
Which battery lasts longer?
The Elite 100 V2 is rated for 4,000+ cycles vs 3,000 for the AC180.
Do both have 5-year warranties?
Yes.
